name: Meunim
overview: Meunim is a male descendant of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role is specifically noted in the context of the temple, emphasizing his service in the religious life of Israel. Beyond his Levitical lineage and temple service, there are no additional personal details recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Meunim means 'people of Maon.' This proper name is not indicated as given by God but reflects a geographical or tribal association. The name itself does not carry additional theological significance beyond identifying this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Meunim as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the Levitical tribe known for priestly and temple duties. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this tribal affiliation and his role as a temple servant.
scriptureSignificance: Meunim's significance lies in his service as a temple servant within the Levitical tribe, highlighting the ongoing role of Levites in maintaining the worship and functions of the temple. His mention underscores the restoration and organization of temple personnel during the post-exilic period, reflecting God's provision for orderly worship. Though not a prominent figure individually, Meunim represents faithful service to God through temple ministry.
